summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted due to hyperglycemia and mechanical falls in the setting of multiple myeloma and chemotherapy. He presented with blood glucose levels in the 500s, poor oral intake, and worsening peripheral neuropathy leading to multiple falls. His long-acting insulin had been discontinued months prior, contributing to poor glycemic control. He received a platelet transfusion for thrombocytopenia and was restarted on glargine insulin with improved glucose levels. A CT head and chest X-ray showed no acute abnormalities. MRI of the spine revealed a stable T12 compression fracture and degenerative changes without cord compression. He received Velcade chemotherapy during admission. His anticoagulation was held due to low platelets and to be resumed outpatient. He was discharged home with a rolling walker, home health services, and follow-up appointments with his oncologist, endocrinologist, and primary care provider.
